summary: Christian Lassen was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and under August Wilhelm von Schlegel at the University of Bonn (Ph.D. 1821–1827). He served at Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and full professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Macalester College, Harvard University, and Columbia University (Ph.D. c. 1996–2003). He taught at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) and became South Asia Center Director at the University of Washington (2007).

Christian Lindtner was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982. He also served as a professor at the University of Copenhagen (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Vienna (1998), curated at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2012), and became David L. Snellgrove Senior Lecturer at SOAS in 2014.
Christian Mabel Duff was a scholar in Indology who studied at Kiel University under Paul Deussen from circa 1892 to 1894.

Christian Matthias Boehm studied biochemistry at TU Munich, biology at Imperial College London, computing at Cambridge, and completed a PhD under Toshifumi Konno at SOAS. He held posts at the Max Planck Institute (2017–2018) and the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (2019).

Christian Schweigaard Stang was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Oslo under Sten Konow and Antoine Meillet. He served at the University of Oslo as Associate Professor (1930) and Professor of Slavic Philology (1938–1970).

Christian Wittern works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields, having studied under Seizan Yanagida. He served as an Associate Researcher at the Chunghwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (1998–2001) and as a professor at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2012).

Christian von Ehrenfels was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna (c. 1878–1885) and the University of Graz (c. 1885–1887). He held posts at the University of Vienna (c. 1888–1896) and as Professor of Philosophy at the German University in Prague (c. 1896–1929).

Christian-Friedrich von Graefe was a linguist who earned his doctorate at Leipzig University (1805). He held chairs in Greek and Latin at the Main Pedagogical Institute, a professorship at Saint Petersburg Theological Academy (1810), and was Conservator and Honorary Director at the State Hermitage Museum.

Christiane Papa-Kalantari works in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After training at the Austrian National Library and working as a research fellow at the University of Vienna (2003–2006), she became an FWF Project Director and postdoctoral researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (2025).

Christiane Strothmann is active in Tibetology and other fields. She served as an Artist in Progress (2016–2018) and lecturer (2024–2026) at Folkwang University of the Arts, and as a lecturer at the University of Paderborn (2023–2026).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, a linguist and Indologist, studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern and Pieter Jacob Cosijn at Leiden University (Ph.D. 1888). He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).
Christine Henriëtte Raabe was an Indology scholar who earned her Ph.D. at Utrecht University (c. 1904–1911), studying under Johan Hendrik Gallée and doctoral supervisor Willem Caland.

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié. She worked as a researcher and Director of Research at the CNRS (1989–1995, attested 2006, 2014) and visited the University of Chicago.

Christmas Humphreys was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Malvern College and Trinity Hall. He founded the Buddhist Society in 1924 and served as its President from circa 1924 to 1983.

Christoph Anderl is a Sinologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and completed his PhD under Christoph Harbsmeier at the University of Oslo (c. 1997–2004). He became a permanent member at Ghent University (c. 2012).

Christoph Cüppers specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (c. 1977–1983) under Lambert Schmithausen, Albrecht Wezler, and S. A. Srinivasan, and served as Director of the Lumbini International Research Institute (c. 1994–2013).

Christoph Emmrich is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who completed doctorates at the Free University of Berlin, University of Tübingen, and Heidelberg University under Axel Michaels. He held posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto (Assistant Professor, 2006).
